judgment.observations: The reconstruction captures the workshop theme, wall shelves, overhead squares, left window and crowded foreground bench. Framing differs: the reference has an oblique, densely filled view, while the reconstruction centers the back wall and leaves more bare upper wall. Shelf tools are smaller, more uniform and repetitive; the reference has varied planes, handles, blades and irregular silhouettes. Many distinctive wall tools and foreground implements are omitted or simplified. The foreground bowl is larger and farther right, and the bench clutter has less overlap. Shelf and bench contacts look more orderly, with several tools appearing embedded in rows. Materials are flatter and cleaner: wood lacks the reference’s aged grain and wear, metal lacks its varied sheen and patina, and the render has conspicuous grainy noise. Overall layout is recognizable, but object fidelity, density and surface character differ substantially.
judgment.uncertain_3d_hypotheses: The rendered room appears shallower and more frontal, and the bench-to-wall spacing may differ, but camera perspective could explain these impressions. Some repeated shelf tools appear to intersect their supports, though occlusion and render noise prevent confirming contact or penetration. No hidden geometry or structural correctness can be assessed.
